memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"That day the LORD saved Israel from the hands of the Egyptians, and Israel saw
the Egyptians lying dead on the shore. And when the Israelites saw the mighty
hand of the LORD displayed against the Egyptians, the people feared the LORD and
put their trust in him and in Moses his servant." - Ex 14:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with three words about the people: they saw, they feared,
they trusted.

Notice the subject of the first sentence: "the LORD saved Israel." Not Moses,
not the wind, not their own courage. The whole chapter has been driving toward
this line.

The fear mentioned here is not terror. It is awe, the right response of small
creatures who have just watched the living God act. Proverbs 9:10 calls the fear
of the LORD the beginning of wisdom. It is not being frightened of God. It is
taking Him seriously.

But here is the honest part, and we should say it. This trust did not last long.
Three days later they would be grumbling about water (Ex 15:22-24). Weeks later
they would want to go back to Egypt. Feelings produced by a great experience fade
faster than we expect.

That is not a reason to despise the moment. It is a reason to build habits that
carry us when the feeling passes, and above all to remember that our security
rests on God's faithfulness, not on the durability of our own devotion.

He brought them through anyway. He kept going with them for forty years.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done for you that you responded to strongly and then forgot?
2. What habit could help you hold on to truth when the feeling fades?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You for saving me. When the feeling of this moment fades, hold me by
Your faithfulness rather than by my own. Amen.
